title: Proactive Microbatch Pressure Regulator with KV-aware Admission
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Summary:
Sustained high QPS workloads are triggering cascading resource pressure in the serving runtime: microbatch admission spikes (larger microbatches), KV-cache thrashing, and periodic GPU memory exhaustion leading to request failures and p95/p99 latency spikes. Current admission logic reacts to instantaneous queue depth and simple CPU/GPU free memory signals; it does not account for KV footprint per-request, short-term QPS trends, nor the cost of enlarging a microbatch (increased KV memory + temporary KV-copy overhead).

Goal:
Design and implement a proactive admission "pressure regulator" that smooths microbatch growth under rising QPS by predicting short-window memory pressure and throttling admission earlier, while coordinating with KV eviction heuristics and autoscaler signals to avoid hard OOMs and large latencies. The regulator must preserve throughput for latency-sensitive customers where possible and degrade predictably (soft-shed, route to variants) for best-effort traffic.

Requirements / Constraints:
- Keep end-to-end 95th and 99th percentile token latency within existing SLOs for standard-tier models during bursts.
- Avoid GPU OOMs and high-frequency KV evictions that increase latency variance.
- Minimize throughput loss compared to current max-throughput behavior.
- Backwards-compatible: feature gated per-pool and per-model; allow opt-out.
- Observable: provide new metrics (see Acceptance Criteria).

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Short-term predictive headroom estimator:
   - Maintain an exponential moving window of arrival rate (1s, 5s, 30s buckets) + microbatch completion rate.
   - Estimate per-request average KV footprint (bytes) and expected KV growth when microbatch size increases (KV-coalescing overhead).
   - Combine with per-GPU memory budget and reserved safety headroom to compute a predicted free-memory curve over the next 5–30s.

2) Admission "pressure regulator" component in front of microbatcher:
   - Instead of a fixed microbatch cap, compute an admission score per request: score = f(current_q, predicted_headroom, request_kv_est, priority).
   - If score < threshold -> delay admission (short backoff) or soft-shed (route to cheaper model variant / fallback path) depending on request priority and customer tier.
   - Use hysteresis to prevent oscillations (upper/lower thresholds + minimum hold time).

3) KV-aware admission and dynamic microbatch ceiling:
   - Tag active requests with estimated KV-size (fast heuristic based on prompt length + cached-prefix hits).
   - Compute microbatch ceiling per-pool as a function of predicted KV memory increase rather than only GPU free memory.
   - Prefer narrow microbatches for KV-heavy requests, allow larger microbatches for short prompts.

4) Coordinated KV eviction policy improvements:
   - Implement KV priority buckets (hot/prefetch/warm) and evict from warm first.
   - When pressure regulator predicts sustained pressure, switch eviction to aggressive compression and demote prefetch entries to disk-backed compressed store.

5) Autoscaler and pool orchestration integration:
   - Emit early "proactive_pressure" signal to autoscaler to pre-warm extra workers when predicted headroom falls below threshold for >15s.
   - When autoscaler cannot provision fast enough, regulator raises soft-shed rate gradually.

6) Fallback & customer-facing behavior:
   - For enterprise/dedicated customers with reserved capacity, prefer autoscaler and pre-warming; only soft-shed if reserve exhausted.
   - For hosted tiers, return well-defined 429 with Retry-After or route to cheaper model variant with metadata describing degradation.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): Implement headroom estimator + new metrics; unit tests for estimator correctness; small benchmarking harness to compare predicted vs real memory curve.
- Phase 2 (3 weeks): Implement admission regulator with simple thresholding and per-request KV estimation; run load tests in staging on canary pool.
- Phase 3 (2 weeks): Add KV-priority buckets and demotion-to-compressed-store code path; integrate with admission regulator decisions.
- Phase 4 (2 weeks): Autoscaler signal integration + rollout plan; extend telemetry and dashboards; prepare runbook.

Trade-offs & alternatives considered:
- Reactive hard-shed on OOM vs predictive soft-shed: predictive soft-shed reduces p99 latency spikes but may reduce peak throughput slightly. We prioritize SLO stability over absolute peak throughput for this feature.
- Per-request exact KV measurement (expensive) vs heuristic estimation: we use heuristics (prompt length, model tokens, cache hit indicator) to keep admission cheap.
- Eviction to compressed disk-backed store vs aggressive in-memory eviction: disk demotion preserves useful KV entries at higher latency cost; combined with admission this keeps p95 stable.

Metrics to track (new):
- proactive_headroom_estimate_bytes (gauge per-worker)
- predicted_vs_actual_memory_error_ratio (histogram)
- regulator_delay_count / regulator_soft_shed_count (counter)
- microbatch_size_distribution_by_kv_bucket (histogram)
- kv_eviction_rate_by_bucket (counter)
- p50/p95/p99 token latency per-pool during regulator on/off A/B tests

Safety & rollout:
- Feature-flagged per-pool; default OFF for top 5 production pools.
- Canary rollout to isolated staging pools, then to a low-traffic hosted pool for 48h.
- Metric-based gating: cannot proceed if p95 increases >10% or successful throughput drops >15% relative to baseline for protected customers.

Acceptance criteria (see separate list):
- New headroom estimator shows <20% median error vs actual memory curve in staging at 5s and 30s horizons.
- During a synthetic high-QPS test, p99 latency decreases by at least 25% vs current reactive system and no GPU OOMs are observed.
- Soft-shed behavior is exercised and clients receive clear retry/variant metadata.

Notes / open questions:
- Need telemetry to measure per-request KV footprint for model families (cost to enable: ~2% overhead). Approve? (see comment thread).
- How aggressively should private/dedicated pools be allowed to pre-empt soft-shed? Proposal: respect contract+reserved headroom flag.
- Coordination with billing/quota: if we route to cheaper variant, should that be counted differently in billing? Ask Product.

Regulator metrics present on console dashboard and alerts configured
